tldr: OFFICEBENCH is one of the first office automation benchmarks evaluating LLM agents' ability to handle realistic multi-application workflows; GPT-4 Omni achieves the highest pass rate of 47.00%, still far below human performance.
contributions: Introduced OFFICEBENCH, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in realistic office automation across multiple applications
Designed a multi-application environment with 9 applications (Word, Excel, PDF, Calendar, Email, OCR, ChatGPT, Shell, System) and a large combined action space
Proposed customized evaluation methods including exact matching, fuzzy matching, and execution-based evaluation tailored to each task
Annotated 300 tasks across Single App (93), Two Apps (95), and Three Apps (112) categories
Evaluated state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini-1.0, Gemini-1.5, Llama 3, Qwen 2) and analyzed failure patterns
methods: OFFICEBENCH is implemented in a Docker environment pre-installed with office applications, where LLM agents interact via a transition system: the current application is the state, operations are transitions, and full execution history is provided as observation. Agents operate within a restricted action space specific to the current application plus switch_app and submit operations. Tasks were annotated across three difficulty categories by involving increasing numbers of applications, and synthetic documents/emails/calendar events were generated using ChatGPT and Python random generators. Evaluation uses three customized methods—Exact Matching, Fuzzy Matching, and Execution-Based Evaluation—tailored per task and file format.
results: GPT-4 Omni achieved the highest pass rate of 47.00% among all tested models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini-1.0, Gemini-1.5, Llama 3, Qwen 2), demonstrating decent but insufficient performance for real-world office workflows. Performance was well below human accuracy standards. Failure analysis revealed issues related to operation redundancy, hallucinations, and limitations in switching between multiple applications.
limitations: GPT-4 Omni's pass rate of 47.00% is far below accuracy standards required by real-world office workflows
Current LLM agents struggle with operation redundancy and hallucinations
Agents show limitations in switching between multiple applications
Complex cross-application planning remains challenging for current LLMs
Maximum iteration limit of 50 steps and stagnation detection (5 consecutive repeated operations) may prematurely terminate tasks
